podcast.title: Origin of "Sting" Name
podcast.body: The band's leader, Gordon Solomon, gave Gordon Sumner the nickname "Sting." This came about because Sumner was known to wear a striped yellow and black jumper, which Solomon said made him look like a bee or a wasp. "The Jasmine's band leader, Gordon Solomon, said the sweater made Sumner look like a bee or a wasp and he began teasing him by calling him Sting."

podcast.title: Sting's Jazz Work
podcast.body: While working as a teacher, Gordon Sumner moonlighted as a jazz musician, playing bass with this troupe, which specialized in "traditional or trad, pre-war New Orleans style jazz." "While teaching, Gordon moonlighted as a jazz musician, playing bass with not only the aforementioned Newcastle Big Band, but also a troupe called the Phoenix Jasmine, which specialized in traditional or trad, pre-war New Orleans style jazz."
